turns.patient_opening: I’m 54, and today I came in because I have pain in my lower chest, mostly on the right side—like a knife-stab type pain. I also feel significant shortness of breath and palpitations, and I’ve had more general vague discomfort and muscle aches since I recently had a viral infection. I’ve also noticed I get worse when I lie flat (orthopnea).

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever been diagnosed with pericarditis (inflammation of the lining around the heart)?
turns.patient_answer: No, I haven’t been diagnosed with pericarditis before. This is the first time I’ve had symptoms like this.

turns.doctor_question: Do you have heart failure (a condition where the heart can’t pump blood as well as it should)?
turns.patient_answer: No, I haven’t been told I have heart failure. I just feel very short of breath and worse when I lie flat, but I don’t have a diagnosis like that.

turns.doctor_question: Does your thoracic spine pain spread or radiate to another area—such as your chest, ribs, shoulder, or around to your back? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: No, the pain doesn’t radiate or spread to another area.

turns.doctor_question: Have you recently had any numbness, loss of sensation, or tingling in **both your arms and legs**, or **around your mouth**?
turns.patient_answer: No, I don’t have numbness, tingling, or loss of sensation around my mouth or in both my arms and legs.

turns.doctor_question: Do you have pain that gets worse when you move (for example, when you walk, turn, or use the affected area)?
turns.patient_answer: No, I wouldn’t say it gets worse when I move like that. It’s more the sharp chest pain plus the breathing symptoms.

turns.doctor_question: Does your pain spread or radiate to another area—such as your back or the right side of your chest wall? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: No, it doesn’t spread or radiate beyond the right side of my chest.
